question: Prakhar and Riya together invested ₹31,600 in a business. At the end of the year, out of a total profit of ₹7,900, Prakhar's share was ₹1,400. What was the investment of Prakhar?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit ratio = Investment ratio

Prakhar : Riya = 1400 : (7900 − 1400) = 1400 : 6500

= 14 : 65

Total ratio = 79 ⇒ Prakhar share = (14/79) × 31600

**∴ Answer = 5600**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total investment = 31600, Total profit = 7900, Prakhar's profit = 1400

**Formula used:**

Profit ratio = Investment ratio (when time is same)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Riya's profit = 7900 − 1400 = 6500

⇒ Profit ratio (Prakhar : Riya) = 1400 : 6500

⇒ Divide both by 100 ⇒ 14 : 65

⇒ Investment ratio = 14 : 65

⇒ Total parts = 14 + 65 = 79

⇒ Prakhar's investment = (14 ÷ 79) × 31600

⇒ = 14 × 400 = 5600

**∴ The correct answer is 5600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Partnership Rule

Profit share ∝ Investment × Time

Equal Time Case

If time is same, Profit ratio = Investment ratio

Ratio Conversion

Simplify ratio by dividing by common factor

Direct Formula

Individual investment = (Individual profit ÷ Total profit) × Total investment
